topic: The π-Collision Mystery: From Bouncing Blocks to Digits of Pi

sections.title: The Hook: The Bouncing Blocks Puzzle
lecture_lines: Two blocks slide toward each other.
Small block hits a massive block.
animations: Fade in two blocks, small and large, on a #FFFFFF line.
Animate the small block moving toward the large block.
Animate the small block bouncing off the large block.
Display the collision counter incrementing from 0 to 1.
Show the blocks moving apart with velocity labels in #00FF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Conservation of Momentum and Energy
lecture_lines: Collisions conserve both energy and momentum.
This reveals a surprising geometric connection.
animations: Show the momentum equation p = mv in #FFFF00.
Show the energy equation E = 1/2mv^2 in #FF00FF.
Draw a circular arc representing conservation constraints in #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Geometric Bridge: Mapping Collisions to Angles
lecture_lines: Each collision is an angular rotation.
Mass ratio sets the arc angle.
Collisions map to digits of pi.
animations: Draw a large unit circle centered on screen in #FFFFFF.
Place a velocity vector rotating around the circle in #FF0000.
Animate the vector rotation corresponding to collision angle theta.
Show arc length S = r*theta growing with collisions in #00FF00.
Label the final arc length as proportional to Pi.

sections.title: The Connection: Why Pi?
animations: Display the mass ratio m1/m2 numerically in #FFFF00.
Show Pi's digits appearing one by one as collisions happen.
Flash the relationship between mass ratio and Pi digits.

sections.title: Summary and Implications
animations: Display a summary diagram of block-circle duality in #00FFFF.
Show Pi = 3.1415... growing from the block simulation.
Fade out all elements leaving only the Pi symbol.
